scope: Source-backed findings beyond the initial eight data cases and reasoning.js. Evidence/Synthesis review is complete for 481 target records (277 Command of Evidence and 204 Rhetorical Synthesis); this findings list is selective and does not cover other bank skills.

findings.title: Weakening an identification does not identify its rival
findings.finding: B makes both jellyfish and ctenophore identification inconclusive. That weakens the claimed ctenophore identity without proving jellyfish. A comparative preservation advantage alone (D) does not establish inability to identify.

findings.title: Test the exact relationship, not a nearby topic
findings.finding: Art–reality relationships differ when one theory permits hypothetical realities not already existing. Shared audience psychology or word history does not answer the translation claim.

findings.title: An adaptation explanation needs a trait-specific resource advantage
findings.finding: Different available prey alone does not explain smaller size. Access to shallow foraging areas inaccessible to larger whales supplies the missing size-to-benefit mechanism.

findings.title: Normalized baseline and significance are separate from bar height
findings.finding: Graph axis notes differences from baseline were not statistically significant. A visual bar above 100% does not establish significant rebound. Source rationale’s “all seals” and “prolonged period” expectations are stronger than the definition supplied; retain the tentative “may not” conclusion and keyed A.

findings.title: Marine reptiles become mammals in one rationale sentence
findings.finding: Correct-answer rationale says “nonendothermic marine mammals” where passage and C say marine reptiles. This is a noun slip; key C remains supported.

findings.title: B states the result but omits the study
findings.finding: Source rejection says B “doesn’t include the study’s findings” despite B giving 74 Orchidaceae species. The supported reason is its failure to present the study. A supplies study attribution and result; key unchanged.

findings.title: Emphasis depends on sentence structure, not fact presence
findings.finding: B mentions different topics but ends on shared influence; A concedes shared effect before foregrounding autobiography versus fiction. For an emphasis goal, merely containing a true difference is insufficient.

findings.title: Historical context requires the claim plus its intellectual setting
findings.finding: A links Einstein’s independent reality claim to the field’s emergence and subsequent acceptance of the rival view. A date or famous debate alone does not give the requested argument in context.

findings.title: Cross-check every requested outcome against the same focal group
findings.finding: D compares positive versus both controls for enjoyment and endurance. A’s endurance comparison leaves positive feedback out, so cannot establish absence of its physical effect.

findings.title: Carrying capacity counts individuals of one species
findings.finding: C says maximum number of species, conflicting with notes’ maximum number of a species. Rationale calls C a definition and rejects only lack of wolf count. Correct instruction: C also misdefines carrying capacity. D remains correct.

findings.title: Challenging priority does not deny accomplishment
findings.finding: Earlier Indigenous fossil discovery would challenge Plot’s being first, not his having found dinosaur remains. Also preserve scope: general dinosaur priority is not priority for M. carinatus specifically.

findings.title: Track the actor and material through a process
findings.finding: A/B/D use process vocabulary but change what passes the dead zone, what is baked, or when curing ends. C preserves UV→resin layers→object oven sequence.

findings.title: The goal determines which source details belong in a narrative opening
findings.finding: Prompt calls VGHS award-nominated to identify its subject, but the requested opening is best served by protagonist, named series, genre, and launch time. A need not repeat the award; outcome-only B jumps past introduction.

findings.title: Stellar mass is not radius
findings.finding: D correctly says SiriusA is more massive than Sun. Source rationale glosses this as larger; retain mass terminology because the notes’ solar masses do not establish radius.

findings.title: Quoted wording must remain exact
findings.finding: D changes notes’ quoted “unsung heroines of the Ghanaian Republic” to “unsung heroes of the Ghanaian Republic.” Source rejection only addresses wrong purpose. It also inaccurately quotes the notes. A remains correct.

findings.title: A concessive clause may contain the requested fact without emphasizing it
findings.finding: D concedes discovery significance with “Though” then foregrounds erroneous hypothesis. A foregrounds significance and consequences; importance merely appearing is not enough.

findings.title: Match the exact comparison axis
findings.finding: Goal asks how GREEN backgrounds are used across countries. A contrasts colors on highways; B holds color fixed and contrasts the road classes receiving it. A true contrast can still answer a nearby question.

findings.title: A valid contrast can use a secondary measured characteristic
findings.finding: D contrasts sample thicknesses rather than main temperature-change results. Broad “contrast samples” goal allows this supported difference; avoid imposing a more specific goal absent from question.

findings.title: Promising potential is not established commercial viability
findings.finding: A reuses quoted words “commercially viable” but changes authors’ conclusion from “promising potential as a commercially viable” crop to marigolds WERE commercially viable. Source rationale only rejects incompleteness. A also overstates conclusion strength. C remains correct.

findings.title: A shared failure can arise from different failed criteria
findings.finding: A groups CTAB2X and Pplant as less effective because each fails at least one of yield/purity. They need not have the same failed metric or matching numerical values. The goal is the significance of their shared inability to meet both criteria.

findings.title: Syllables per second do not measure information per second
findings.finding: B claims information is conveyed faster in Spanish based on 7.7 versus5.3 syllables/sec, though notes distinguish roughly constant information rates from varying syllable rates. Rationale rejects only limited overview; B also conflates metrics. D remains correct.

findings.title: Explain a change with a changing mechanism
findings.finding: D gives current closeness and apparent merging; C specifically says stars moved together since older accounts. To explain appearance change, preserve the temporal movement rather than static condition alone.

findings.title: Choose the requested event sequence, not the investigators’ workflow
findings.finding: D gives proposal→simulation→hypothesis sequence. C gives the physical history proposed in the study, which is the requested target. Same sequence vocabulary can describe the wrong events.

findings.title: A statistic stays attached to its measured outcome and causal direction
findings.finding: D changes99% less hunting time caused by more tuna into99% tuna increase caused by changed hunting. Both the metric and causal arrow must survive synthesis. B also upgrades pending deterrent testing to proven efficacy.

findings.title: At most25% includes sites meeting zero needs
findings.finding: C’s first clause is consistent with the graph:0% and up-to25% sites together exceed80% currently. Its second clause fails because the maximum-temperature >25% bar is about78%, below80%. Source rationale rejects C by listing0% and up-to25% separately without identifying the false second clause. Key D remains correct.

findings.title: Peeling benefit is an answer-choice detail, not a premise
findings.finding: Source rejection of D says Armijo’s hypothesis mentions easier peeling, but the passage only hypothesizes reduced roasting time from more heliostats. Easier peeling appears only in distractor D. Reject D because it measures the wrong outcome; key B remains correct.

findings.title: An indirect effect needs both directional links
findings.finding: B supplies NFM→lower political knowledge/interest and knowledge/interest→higher voting likelihood. Combining those signs supports reduced voting likelihood indirectly; identifying a mediator alone or mentioning network size without directional first link is insufficient. The passage keeps this as may reduce rather than a direct voting experiment.

findings.title: Explain a cost gap with a difference in effects
findings.finding: C links more frequent replacement to repeated higher new-material costs, explaining a widening new-versus-recycled cost gap. B foregrounds rising cumulative costs, which could affect both groups; its concession about potential recycling savings does not draw the needed comparative conclusion. Track total levels separately from the gap between them.

findings.title: Bar differences do not establish statistical significance
findings.finding: Source describes significantly lower metal levels, but graph supplies heights without uncertainty or a test. D describes lower levels and remains supported; avoid statistical-significance claims.

findings.title: Recall decay needs a comparison group
findings.finding: D says sharers forget details after a week; without low-engagement recall at that delay this does not establish weaker relative recall. C directly compares comments and links and remains correct.

findings.title: A cross-species comparison does not test fungal benefit
findings.finding: B compares corn with broccoli in fungal soil. Its rationale instead discusses corn being more massive with fungi, a within-species comparison B never makes. Reject B because species differ independently of treatment; A remains correct.

findings.title: Highest spray efficiency is near17%, not14–16%
findings.finding: Graph places highest spray coating near17%, above16%; source rejection of C incorrectly gives14–16% for that highest bar. Lowest spray~15.5% still exceeds best spin~13.5%, so B remains correct.

findings.title: Algeria exceeds70% in2020
findings.finding: Graph places Algeria near75% in2020. Source repeatedly says reached70%; choice D correctly says more than70%. Preserve the distinction when teaching threshold readings.

findings.title: A trend distractor can also misstate a value
findings.finding: D claims both lakes exceed105days in2005–06; Neusiedl is about100–102, below105. Source rejection only notes the missing before/after comparison and says graph could indicate the claim. C remains correct.

findings.title: All thrum genera change; the direction differs
findings.finding: Source says intact/damaged thrum time differs for only some genera. Table shows differences for all four: Habropoda4.1→9.5,Osmia7.1→8.3,Pierid2.4→1.9,Xylocopa2.5→2.2. A correctly distinguishes increases from decreases; do not equate decreasing with no effect.

findings.title: A force-to-weight claim needs the denominator ratio
findings.finding: The relevant support is that weight ratio is close to1 while force ratio exceeds4. Merely both weighing above450g cannot constrain their ratio. Graph also shows~510and490g rather than source approximation500and480g; keyD unchanged.

findings.title: Reject the choice actually printed
findings.finding: A dates the Fairfield Gorget to the earlier Woodland period; its source rejection instead discusses a Mexican artifact appearing only after the gorget. That artifact is absent from A. A supplies no Mexican-art contact evidence, whereas C supplies a nearby contemporaneous Mexican object. Key C remains supported; PDF page visually checked.

findings.title: A cross-year comparison does not contradict a same-year treatment effect
findings.finding: C accurately compares 2018 control yield with 2019 nitrogen yield. The rationale calls this a strong conflict with nitrogen improving yield, but weather or other year effects can coexist with nitrogen outperforming same-year controls in every year. Reject C because it does not isolate the treatment comparison; retain B. Graph and source rationale card visually checked.

findings.title: Borrowed vocabulary does not establish related language families
findings.finding: The rationale says Caddo is described as closely related to the Totozoquean family. The passage actually proposes cultural contact and borrowing of corn vocabulary through unrelated Chitimacha. A is supported by corn cultivation without demonstrably Totozoquean-derived corn words in Cherokee/Muskogean; do not turn lexical borrowing into a genealogical language relationship. PDF page visually checked.

findings.title: Share of authors differs from share of works
findings.finding: A reports the percentage of Random House AUTHORS who were Black. Its correct-answer rationale paraphrases that as a higher percentage of WORKS by Black authors. Authors can publish different numbers of works, so those denominators are not interchangeable. The author-share increase itself supports the likely representation aim; key A remains supported.

findings.title: Test necessity and insufficiency with two different observations
findings.finding: In the displayed sample every total-outlay decrease occurs during divided Congress, while the divided 1975–1976 period has an increase of 2.7 percentage points. The first pattern supports necessity in this sample; the exception shows division is insufficient. Component defense/nondefense decreases cannot substitute for total outlays. D remains correct; source table visually checked.

findings.title: A knockout label names what is absent
findings.finding: Type A means DptA is silenced and DptB remains active. Its high survival after A. sicerae infection therefore supports a role for DptB, while low survival of B and AB tracks DptB absence. No both-active group is graphed, and only two pathogens are discussed, so do not infer the both-active optimum or universal pathogen exclusivity. C remains correct; source graph visually checked.

findings.title: Use a global upper bound to constrain a local subgroup
findings.finding: Tanzania has 61 million Swahili speakers, while at most 15 million worldwide have Swahili as a first language. Even assigning every first-language speaker to Tanzania leaves at least roughly 46 million later-language speakers there. The proof does not require knowing how native speakers are distributed among countries. A remains correct; source table visually checked.
